sections.html:
Montgomery is the capital of Alabama and the seat of Montgomery County, on the Alabama River. The city had 200,603 residents in 2020, and the metro area had 385,460 in 2022. Daytime population runs to 239,101, about 17.4% above the resident count, because state offices, the air force base and hospitals pull in commuters from nearby counties.

State government, Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base and manufacturing give the city a wide mix of housing. A downtown condo near the Capitol, a mid-century brick ranch on the east side and a farmhouse at the edge of town all sit inside one city limit.

Sellers here tend to land in a few familiar spots. A relative's house is inherited after decades in one neighborhood. A rental has aged past what the owner wants to spend. A transfer to or from the base leaves a firm report date and no time for a long listing.

Government work keeps demand steady, but it also brings turnover. Military families rotate on assignment cycles, and a house that cannot close before a report date turns into a carrying cost in two cities at once.

Hospitals add their own pockets of demand. Baptist Medical Center South, Baptist Medical Center East near Auburn University at Montgomery, and Jackson Hospital beside Oak Park off Interstate 85 each anchor nearby streets. Landlords near those workplaces see the same pattern: tenants follow the workday, not only the resident count.

Montgomery Public Schools serves most of the city, and families often ask which school an address feeds. Magnet programs are part of the system, so school assignment is one factor buyers weigh. Housing on Maxwell Air Force Base is zoned differently, to a Department of Defense school for the lower grades and Montgomery Public Schools for high school.

Montgomery's older neighborhoods sit along former streetcar lines, since residents moved outward along them in the 1880s. A house in one of those areas can be well over a century old, and a buyer's inspector will look hard at structure, wiring and plumbing.

The city adopted a downtown master plan in 2007 covering Court Square, the riverfront and Dexter Avenue, and it uses SmartCode zoning. If you own near downtown, zoning rules may differ from those in the outer subdivisions, so call the city before you assume what a buyer can do with the lot.

sections.h2: What heat and rain do to a house
sections.html:
Summers are long and hot, with highs above 90 on roughly 86 days a year and afternoon heat index readings that often reach 100. The city averages about 51 inches of precipitation a year, and February, March and July are the wettest months. A buyer's inspector knows all of this and checks accordingly:

  • Roofs take months of heat and then spring hail and wind, so roof condition is a standard inspection item.
  • Air conditioning runs hard from May through September, and a failing unit is one of the first things flagged.
  • Humidity near 70 percent on average encourages mold, wood rot and soft spots under sinks and around windows.
  • Severe thunderstorms can bring large hail, and weakened tropical storms can drop heavy rain.

Montgomery also has a tornado history. A storm hit the western part of the city on February 12, 1945. Buyers and insurers may ask about roof age and past claims.

Interstate 65 runs through Montgomery and Interstate 85 ends here. Montgomery Regional Airport has regular flights to Atlanta, Houston and Charlotte. Passenger rail stopped in 1995.

Road access shows up in the price talk. A house a few minutes from an interstate ramp reaches the base, downtown offices and hospitals quickly. A property on a busy arterial or beside a rail line may need more negotiation. A cash buyer weighs those traits the same way a financed buyer does, then folds needed repairs into the offer.

sections.h2: Recording tax and property tax dates
sections.html:

Deed recordation taxPaid before the probate office records the deed50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed
Property tax dueEvery yearOctober 1
Property tax delinquentEvery yearAfter December 31

Alabama collects its deed recordation tax under Alabama Code section 40-22-1. The judge of probate figures it from the actual purchase price, and the deed must come with proof of that price on a form from the Department of Revenue. Only the value above a mortgage that already paid mortgage tax is taxed. A recording fee is added, and your title company or closing attorney can give you the exact total.

Property tax is a separate bill. If you sell in the fall, ask who pays it, because the amount is usually split at closing by the dates in the contract. Call the Montgomery County appraisal and tax offices for your parcel's figures and any exemptions, since those depend on the property and the owner.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Montgomery
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when time or condition is the main problem and the last dollar is not. In Montgomery that usually means one of these:

  • An inherited house with deferred repairs, such as an old roof or failing air conditioning.
  • A rental with a tenant, past-due rent or damage that would scare off financed buyers.
  • A military or state job relocation with a fixed report date.
  • A house with a pending tax bill, code notice or other cost the owner wants to stop.

The steps are short. You share the address and the condition. The buyer makes an offer. If you accept, a title company or closing attorney checks the title, pays off any mortgage or tax bill from the proceeds and sets the closing date. You sign, and funds go out at closing.

For the closing, bring a photo ID, the loan payoff details if there is a mortgage, the latest tax bill, and the lease if a tenant lives there. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, so repairs and cleaning are not required first.

The tradeoff is that an as-is offer usually comes in below a fully repaired retail sale. Compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, commissions and months of carrying costs. We make offers on Montgomery houses, and you are free to say no.

faqs.q: Is Montgomery the capital of Alabama?
faqs.a: Yes. Montgomery became the state capital on January 28, 1846, when the seat of government moved from Tuscaloosa. It is also the county seat of Montgomery County.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. Your county tax office can confirm the amount and the payoff for a closing.

faqs.q: What tax is paid when a deed is recorded in Montgomery?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed under Code section 40-22-1, paid to the probate office before the deed is recorded. A recording fee is added, and the total depends on the sale price.

faqs.q: Does the weather matter when selling a house in Montgomery?
faqs.a: Yes. Long hot summers, spring hail and heavy rain wear roofs, air conditioners and crawl spaces, so inspectors look at them closely. An as-is cash sale means you do not fix them first.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Montgomery house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses in their current condition, including those with old roofs, water damage or deferred maintenance. The offer reflects the repairs the buyer takes on.
